title: Chapter 16 — Galliformes
description: Heavy-bodied, ground-dwelling birds built for short bursts of flight rather than sustained soaring. Galliformes gave us almost all domestic poultry — chickens, turkeys, guinea fowl, and quail — and include the spectacular peafowl and pheasants.

children.name: Afropavo
children.description: A monotypic African genus containing the Congo Peafowl, the only peafowl native to Africa, found in the dense lowland rainforests of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

children.name: Afropavo congensis
children.description: The Congo peafowl (Afropavo congensis), also known as the African peafowl or mbulu by the Bakôngo, is a species native to the Congo Basin.

children.name: Alectoris
children.description: A genus of 7 rock-partridge species distributed across southern Europe, the Middle East, and Central Asia, characterized by bold facial and flank markings and a preference for rocky, arid hillsides.

children.name: Alectoris barbara
children.description: The Barbary partridge (Alectoris barbara) is a gamebird in the pheasant family (Phasianidae) of the order Galliformes.

children.name: Alectoris chukar
children.description: The chukar partridge, or simply chukar, is a Palearctic upland gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae. It has been considered to form a superspecies complex along with the rock partridge, Philby's partridge and Przevalski's partridge and treated in the past as conspecific particularly with the first. This partridge has well-marked black and white bars on the flanks and a black band running from the forehead across the eye down the head to form a necklace that encloses a white throat.

children.name: Alectoris graeca
children.description: The rock partridge or common rock partridge (Alectoris graeca) is a gamebird in the pheasant family, Phasianidae, of the order Galliformes (gallinaceous birds).

children.name: Alectoris melanocephala
children.description: The Arabian partridge (Alectoris melanocephala) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae, native to the southern Arabian Peninsula.

children.name: Ammoperdix
children.description: A genus of 2 sand-partridge species adapted to arid and semi-arid rocky deserts from the Sinai and Middle East east to Pakistan, notable for their cryptic sandy plumage.

children.name: Ammoperdix heyi
children.description: thumb|Illustration depicting the plumage of a male sand partridge.

children.name: Arborophila
children.description: A genus of roughly 20 hill-partridge species confined to the forest understory of South and Southeast Asia, typically identified by colorful throat and breast patterns and a reluctance to fly.

children.name: Arborophila ardens
children.description: The Hainan partridge (Arborophila ardens) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Arborophila campbelli
children.description: The Malayan partridge (Arborophila campbelli), also known as the Malay partridge, Malaysian partridge, Malay hill partridge or Campbell's partridge, is a bird species in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Arborophila crudigularis
children.description: The Taiwan partridge or Taiwan hill partridge (Arborophila crudigularis) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Arborophila rufipectus
children.description: The Sichuan partridge (Arborophila rufipectus) is a bird species in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Arborophila sumatrana
children.description: The Sumatran partridge, or Sumatran hill partridge, (Arborophila sumatrana) is a bird species in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Arborophila torqueola
children.description: The common hill partridge, necklaced hill partridge, or simply hill partridge (Arborophila torqueola) is a species of bird in the pheasant family found in Asia.

children.name: Argusianus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Great Argus, a large pheasant of the lowland rainforests of Borneo and the Malay Peninsula, renowned for the male's enormously elongated secondary wing feathers covered in eye-like ocelli used in elaborate courtship displays.

children.name: Argusianus argus
children.description: The great argus (Argusianus argus), or greater argus, is a large species of pheasant from Southeast Asia.

children.name: Bambusicola
children.description: A genus of 3 bamboo-partridge species from South and East Asia, including the familiar Chinese Bamboo Partridge, typically found in bamboo thickets and dense scrub at forest edges.

children.name: Bonasa
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Ruffed Grouse, a forest grouse of North America's deciduous and mixed woodlands, best known for the male's drumming display produced by rapid wing-beats.

children.name: Bonasa umbellus
children.description: ]] The ruffed grouse (Bonasa umbellus) is a medium-sized grouse occurring in forests from the Appalachian Mountains across Canada to Alaska.

children.name: Caloperdix
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Ferruginous Partridge, a secretive, rufous-and-black-spotted forest partridge of the Thai–Malay Peninsula and Borneo.

children.name: Caloperdix oculeus
children.description: The ferruginous partridge (Caloperdix oculeus) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Campocolinus
children.description: A small genus of 3 African francolins found in sub-Saharan savanna and grassland habitats, separated from the larger Francolinus complex based on molecular evidence.

children.name: Campocolinus coqui
children.description: The Coqui francolin (Campocolinus coqui) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Canachites
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Spruce Grouse, a tame and well-camouflaged North American grouse specialized for coniferous forest habitats, subsisting heavily on pine and spruce needles in winter.

children.name: Canachites canadensis
children.description: The spruce grouse (Canachites canadensis), also known as Canada grouse, spruce hen or fool hen, is a medium-sized grouse closely associated with the coniferous boreal forests or taiga of North America.

children.name: Catreus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Cheer Pheasant, a vulnerable long-tailed pheasant of steep grassy and scrubby hillsides in the western Himalayas from Pakistan to northwestern India.

children.name: Catreus wallichii
children.description: The cheer pheasant (Catreus wallichii), also known as Wallich's pheasant or chir pheasant, is a vulnerable species of the pheasant family, Phasianidae.

children.name: Centrocercus
children.description: A genus of 2 sage-grouse species endemic to the sagebrush steppes of western North America, the largest North American grouse, famous for spectacular lekking displays at communal grounds.

children.name: Centrocercus minimus
children.description: The Gunnison grouse, Gunnison sage-grouse or lesser sage-grouse (Centrocercus minimus) is a species of grouse endemic to the United States.

children.name: Centrocercus urophasianus
children.description: The greater sage-grouse (Centrocercus urophasianus), also known as the sagehen, is the largest grouse in North America.

children.name: Chrysolophus
children.description: A genus of 2 spectacularly colored ruffed pheasants from the mountain forests of central China, comprising the Golden Pheasant and Lady Amherst's Pheasant, both widely kept in aviculture worldwide.

children.name: Chrysolophus pictus
children.description: The golden pheasant (Chrysolophus pictus), also known as the Chinese pheasant, and rainbow pheasant, is a gamebird of the order Galliformes (gallinaceous birds) and the family Phasianidae (pheasants).

children.name: Coturnix
children.description: A genus of 4–5 true quail species distributed across Europe, Africa, and Asia, including the migratory Common Quail and the domesticated Japanese Quail widely used in research and food production.

children.name: Coturnix coromandelica
children.description: thumb|In [[Bhigwan, Maharashtra, India.]] thumb|Drawing of the head of a rain quail The rain quail or black-breasted quail (Coturnix coromandelica) is a species of quail found in the Indian Sub-continent and South-east Asia; its range including Pakistan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.

children.name: Coturnix coturnix
children.description: The common quail or European quail is a small ground-nesting game bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae. It is mainly migratory, breeding in the western Palearctic and wintering in Africa and southern India.

children.name: Coturnix delegorguei
children.description: The harlequin quail (Coturnix delegorguei) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Coturnix japonica
children.description: The Japanese quail (Coturnix japonica), also known as the coturnix quail, is a species of Old World quail found in East Asia.

children.name: Coturnix pectoralis
children.description: The stubble quail (Coturnix pectoralis), whose other common names include grey quail and pectoral quail, is a species of Old World quail native to Australia.

children.name: Crossoptilon
children.description: A genus of 4 eared-pheasant species native to the high-altitude forests and scrub of central China and Tibet, recognized by their velvety plumage, red facial skin, and distinctive ear-like white cheek tufts.

children.name: Crossoptilon crossoptilon
children.description: The white eared pheasant (Crossoptilon crossoptilon), also known as Dolan's eared pheasant or Bee's pheasant, is a species of "eared pheasant" that get its name because its colouration is white and has the prominent ear tufts of the genus, not because it has white ears.

children.name: Dendragapus
children.description: A genus of 2 blue-grouse species—the Dusky and Sooty Grouse—inhabiting montane coniferous forests along the Pacific coast and Rocky Mountains of western North America.

children.name: Dendragapus fuliginosus
children.description: The sooty grouse (Dendragapus fuliginosus) is a species of forest-dwelling grouse native to North America's Pacific Coast Ranges.

children.name: Dendragapus obscurus
children.description: The dusky grouse (Dendragapus obscurus) is a species of forest-dwelling grouse native to the Rocky Mountains in North America.

children.name: Falcipennis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Siberian Grouse, a small, dark forest grouse of the taiga zone from the Russian Far East through Siberia, closely related to the Spruce Grouse of North America.

children.name: Falcipennis falcipennis
children.description: The Siberian grouse (Falcipennis falcipennis), also known as Siberian spruce grouse, Amur grouse, or Asian spruce grouse, is a short, rotund forest-dwelling grouse.

children.name: Francolinus
children.description: A genus of 3 francolins found from sub-Saharan Africa through South and Southeast Asia, including the Black Francolin, characterized by boldly patterned plumage and loud, far-carrying calls.

children.name: Francolinus francolinus
children.description: The black francolin (Francolinus francolinus) is a gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes.

children.name: Francolinus pictus
children.description: The painted francolin or painted partridge (Francolinus pictus) is a species of francolin found in grassy areas in central and southern India and in the lowlands of southeastern Sri Lanka.

children.name: Francolinus pintadeanus
children.description: The Chinese francolin (Francolinus pintadeanus) or Burmese francolin is a species of game bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Galloperdix
children.description: A genus of 3 spurfowl species endemic to the Indian subcontinent, distinguished by the males' multiple leg spurs and their preference for dense forest undergrowth.

children.name: Galloperdix lunulata
children.description: The painted spurfowl (Galloperdix lunulata) is a bird of the pheasant family found in rocky hill and scrub forests mainly in peninsular India.

children.name: Galloperdix spadicea
children.description: The red spurfowl (Galloperdix spadicea) is a member of the pheasant family and is endemic to India.

children.name: Gallus
children.description: A genus of 4 junglefowl species native to South and Southeast Asia, including the Red Junglefowl (Gallus gallus), the wild ancestor of the domestic chicken and arguably the most economically important bird in human history.

children.name: Gallus gallus
children.description: The red junglefowl, also known as the Indian red junglefowl, is a species of tropical, galliform bird in the phasianid family, found across much of Southeast Asia and parts of South Asia.

children.name: Gallus gallus domesticus
children.description: Gallus gallus domesticus (Domestic Chicken) is a junglefowl species found in its native habitat.

children.name: Gallus sonneratii
children.description: The grey junglefowl (Gallus sonneratii), also known as Sonnerat's junglefowl, is one of the wild ancestors of the domestic chicken together with the red junglefowl and other junglefowls.

children.name: Gallus varius
children.description: The green junglefowl (Gallus varius), also known as Javan junglefowl, forktail or green Javanese junglefowl, is the most distantly related and the first to diverge at least 4 million years ago among the four species of the junglefowl.

children.name: Haematortyx
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Crimsonhead Partridge, a little-known, blood-red-headed partridge confined to montane forest in Borneo.

children.name: Ithaginis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Blood Pheasant, a small, partridge-like pheasant of high-altitude Himalayan and Tibetan conifer and rhododendron forests, with the male's striking crimson-and-green plumage.

children.name: Ithaginis cruentus
children.description: The blood pheasant (Ithaginis cruentus) or blood partridge is a galliforme bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae and the only species in the genus Ithaginis.

children.name: Lagopus
children.description: A genus of 3 ptarmigan species adapted to Arctic and alpine tundra across the Northern Hemisphere, uniquely among grouse molting into pure-white plumage each winter for camouflage in snow.

children.name: Lagopus lagopus
children.description: The willow ptarmigan is a bird in the grouse tribe Tetraonini of the pheasant family Phasianidae. It is also known as the willow grouse. The willow ptarmigan breeds in birch and other forests and moorlands in northern Europe, the tundra of Scandinavia, Siberia, Alaska, and Canada, in particular in the provinces of Newfoundland and Labrador and Quebec.

children.name: Lerwa
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Snow Partridge, a finely barred and rufous-tailed partridge of the high-altitude rocky slopes and alpine meadows of the Himalayas and Tibetan Plateau.

children.name: Lerwa lerwa
children.description: The snow partridge (Lerwa lerwa) is a gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae found widely distributed across the high-altitude Himalayan regions of Pakistan, China, India and Nepal.

children.name: Lophophorus
children.description: A genus of 3 monal pheasant species inhabiting alpine forests and meadows of the Himalayas and adjacent ranges, the males being among the most brilliantly iridescent of all birds.

children.name: Lophophorus impejanus
children.description: The Himalayan monal (Lophophorus impejanus), also called Impeyan monal, is a landfowl native to Himalayan forests and shrublands at elevations of .

children.name: Lophophorus lhuysii
children.description: The Chinese monal or Chinese impeyan (Lophophorus lhuysii) is a species in the pheasant family Phasianidae native to west-central China, where it is restricted to the mountains of western Sichuan and southern Gansu.

children.name: Lophura
children.description: A diverse genus of about 12 pheasant species found across South and Southeast Asia, including the Silver Pheasant and Kalij Pheasant, typically featuring males with iridescent blue-black plumage, red facial wattles, and elaborate tails.

children.name: Lophura diardi
children.description: The Siamese fireback (Lophura diardi), also known as Diard's fireback, is a fairly large, approximately long, pheasant.

children.name: Lophura leucomelanos
children.description: The kalij pheasant (Lophura leucomelanos), or simply kalij, is a pheasant found in forests and thickets, especially in the Himalayan foothills, from Nepal, Pakistan to western Thailand.

children.name: Lophura nycthemera
children.description: The silver pheasant (Lophura nycthemera) is a species of pheasant found in forests, mainly in mountains, of mainland Southeast Asia and eastern and southern China.

children.name: Lyrurus
children.description: A genus of 2 black grouse species from Eurasia—the widespread Black Grouse and the Caucasian Grouse—known for their lyre-shaped tails and communal lek displays on open heathlands and forest edges.

children.name: Lyrurus mlokosiewiczi
children.description: thumb|Illustration The Caucasian grouse or Caucasian black grouse (Lyrurus mlokosiewiczi) is a large bird in the grouse tribe.

children.name: Lyrurus tetrix
children.description: The black grouse, also known as northern black grouse, Eurasian black grouse, blackgame or blackcock, is a large bird in the grouse tribe. It is a sedentary species, spanning across the Palearctic in moorland and steppe habitat when breeding, often near wooded areas. They will spend the winter perched in dense forests, feeding almost exclusively on the needles of conifers.

children.name: Margaroperdix
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Madagascar Partridge, an endemic ground-dwelling partridge of Madagascar's grasslands and scrubby hillsides.

children.name: Margaroperdix madagarensis
children.description: The Madagascar partridge (Margaroperdix madagarensis) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Melanoperdix
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Black Partridge, a small, nearly all-black forest partridge restricted to lowland rainforests of the Malay Peninsula and Borneo.

children.name: Melanoperdix niger
children.description: The black partridge (Melanoperdix niger), also known as the black wood partridge, is a small (up to 27 cm long) partridge with a thick bill, grey legs and dark brown iris.

children.name: Meleagris
children.description: A genus of 2 turkey species native to North and Central America, including the Wild Turkey (ancestor of the domestic turkey) and the iridescent Ocellated Turkey of the Yucatán Peninsula.

children.name: Meleagris gallopavo
children.description: The wild turkey (Meleagris gallopavo) is an upland game bird native to North America, one of two extant species of turkey and the heaviest member of the order Galliformes.

children.name: Meleagris gallopavo f. domestica
children.description: Meleagris gallopavo f. domestica (Domestic Turkey) is a turkey species found in its native habitat.

children.name: Meleagris ocellata
children.description: The ocellated turkey (Meleagris ocellata) is a species of turkey residing primarily in the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico, as well as in parts of Belize and Guatemala.

children.name: Ortygornis
children.description: A genus of 3 francolins from Africa and South Asia—including the widespread Grey Francolin—inhabiting dry scrub, grassland, and agricultural areas from the Indian subcontinent to East Africa.

children.name: Ortygornis pondicerianus
children.description: The grey francolin (Ortygornis pondicerianus) is a species of francolin found in the plains and drier parts of the Indian subcontinent and Iran.

children.name: Ortygornis sephaena
children.description: The crested francolin (Ortygornis sephaena) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Pavo
children.description: A genus of 2 peafowl species from South and Southeast Asia, including the Indian Peafowl whose male bears the longest tail-train of any bird, used in elaborate fanned courtship displays.

children.name: Pavo cristatus
children.description: The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), also known as the common peafowl, or blue peafowl, is a species of peafowl native to the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Pavo muticus
children.description: The green peafowl (Pavo muticus) is a peafowl species native to the tropical forests of Southeast Asia and Southern China.

children.name: Peliperdix
children.description: A small genus of African francolins (currently treated as 1–2 species) inhabiting forest edges and woodland in central and western Africa, recently split from the broader Francolinus assemblage.

children.name: Perdicula
children.description: A genus of 4 small bush-quail species endemic to the Indian subcontinent, inhabiting open grasslands, scrub, and dry hillsides, and distinguished by their compact size and rapid, whirring flight.

children.name: Perdix
children.description: A genus of 3 true partridge species spread across Europe and Asia, including the Grey Partridge widely hunted as a gamebird, characterized by rotund bodies, orange-buff faces, and a preference for open farmland and steppe.

children.name: Perdix dauurica
children.description: The Daurian partridge (Perdix dauurica), also known as steppe partridge, Asian grey partridge or bearded partridge, is a gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes (gallinaceous birds).

children.name: Perdix hodgsoniae
children.description: The Tibetan partridge (Perdix hodgsoniae) is a gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes.

children.name: Perdix perdix
children.description: The grey partridge (Perdix perdix) is a bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes, gallinaceous birds.

children.name: Phasianus
children.description: A genus of 2 pheasant species—the Common Pheasant and the Green Pheasant—native to Asia, with the highly polytypic Common Pheasant (30 subspecies) introduced as a gamebird across much of the world.

children.name: Phasianus colchicus
children.description: The common pheasant, ring-necked pheasant, or blue-headed pheasant, is a bird in the pheasant family (Phasianidae). The genus name comes from Latin phasianus 'pheasant'. The species name colchicus is Latin for 'of Colchis', a country on the Black Sea where pheasants became known to Europeans.

children.name: Phasianus versicolor
children.description: The green pheasant (Phasianus versicolor), also known as the Japanese green pheasant or Kiji, is an omnivorous bird native to the Japanese archipelago, to which it is endemic.

children.name: Polyplectron
children.description: A genus of 8 peacock-pheasant species from Southeast Asian forests, notable for the dense iridescent ocelli covering the wings and tail that the male fans in display, analogous to but convergent with true peafowl.

children.name: Pternistis
children.description: The largest francolin genus with about 25 species distributed across sub-Saharan Africa, occupying diverse habitats from forest and scrub to open grassland, many species identified by distinctive bare facial skin patches.

children.name: Pternistis ahantensis
children.description: The Ahanta francolin or Ahanta spurfowl (Pternistis ahantensis) is a species of bird in the pheasant family, Phasianidae.

children.name: Pternistis capensis
children.description: The Cape spurfowl or Cape francolin (Pternistis capensis) is a gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.

children.name: Pternistis natalensis
children.description: The Natal spurfowl or Natal francolin (Pternistis natalensis) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Pternistis nobilis
children.description: The handsome spurfowl (Pternistis nobilis) is a species of bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.

children.name: Pternistis ochropectus
children.description: The Djibouti spurfowl or Djibouti francolin (Pternistis ochropectus) is a bird species in the pheasant family, Phasianidae.

children.name: Pternistis squamatus
children.description: The scaly spurfowl (Pternistis squamatus) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Pucrasia
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Koklass Pheasant, a medium-sized, cryptically patterned pheasant of the forested Himalayan and Chinese mountain slopes, notable for its loud, distinctive call.

children.name: Pucrasia macrolopha
children.description: The koklass pheasant (Pucrasia macrolopha) is a species of gamebird, being closely related to progenitive grouse that lived during the Miocene.

children.name: Rheinardia
children.description: A genus of 2 crested-argus species from the mountain forests of Vietnam, Laos, and Borneo, the males bearing extraordinarily long, wide, ocellated tail feathers that rival those of the Great Argus.

children.name: Rheinardia nigrescens
children.description: The Malayan crested argus is a large and spectacular peafowl-like species of bird in the pheasant family with dark-brown-spotted black and buff plumage, a heavy pink bill, brown irises and blue skin around the eyes. The head has two crests; the hind crest, which extends down the occiput, is erected when alarmed and during intentional behaviors including pair bonding and courtship displays. The male has a broad and greatly elongated tail of twelve feathers.

children.name: Rheinardia ocellata
children.description: The Vietnamese crested argus is a large and spectacular peafowl-like species of bird in the pheasant family with dark-brown-spotted black and buff plumage, a heavy pink bill, brown irises and blue skin around the eyes. The head has two crests; the hind crest, which extends down the occiput, is erected when alarmed and during intentional behaviors including pair bonding and courtship displays. The male has a broad and greatly elongated tail of twelve feathers.

children.name: Rhizothera
children.description: A genus of 2 long-billed partridge species from the lowland and montane forests of Borneo and the Malay Peninsula, characterized by their unusually long bills used to probe for invertebrates in leaf litter.

children.name: Rhizothera dulitensis
children.description: The Dulit partridge (Rhizothera dulitensis), also known as Hose's partridge, has been considered a distinctive subspecies of the long-billed partridge, a bird in the Phasianidae, or pheasant, family.

children.name: Rollulus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Crested Partridge (or Roul-roul), a striking forest partridge of the Thai–Malay Peninsula and Borneo, with the male's vivid green-and-red plumage and bristly red crest.

children.name: Rollulus rouloul
children.description: The crested partridge (Rollulus rouloul), also known as the crested wood partridge, roul-roul, red-crowned wood partridge, green wood quail, and green wood partridge is a gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes, gallinaceous birds.

children.name: Scleroptila
children.description: A genus of about 8 African francolins found primarily in southern and eastern Africa, inhabiting highland grasslands and montane scrub, several species being characteristic birds of the highveld.

children.name: Scleroptila elgonensis
children.description: The Elgon francolin (Scleroptila elgonensis) is a francolin found in moorland at altitudes above from eastern Uganda (Mount Elgon) to central Kenya.

children.name: Scleroptila psilolaema
children.description: The moorland francolin (Scleroptila psilolaema) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Synoicus
children.description: A genus of 4 button-quail-like quail species from Africa, South Asia, and Australasia, including the widespread Brown Quail of Australia and New Guinea, occupying grasslands and grassy woodland.

children.name: Synoicus adansonii
children.description: The blue quail or African blue quail (Synoicus adansonii) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae found in sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Synoicus chinensis
children.description: The king quail (Synoicus chinensis), also known as the Asian blue quail, blue-breasted quail, Chinese painted quail, or Chung-Chi, is a very small, diminutive galliform of the tribe Coturnicini in the subfamily Phasianinae.

children.name: Synoicus ypsilophorus
children.description: The brown quail (Synoicus ypsilophorus), also known as the swamp quail, silver quail and Tasmanian quail, is an Australasian true quail of the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Syrmaticus
children.description: A genus of 5 long-tailed pheasants native to the mountain forests of East Asia, including Reeves's Pheasant with the longest tail of any wild bird, and several threatened island endemics.

children.name: Syrmaticus mikado
children.description: thumb|[[China Airlines Airbus A350-900 (B-18901) with Mikado Pheasant livery.]].

children.name: Syrmaticus soemmerringii
children.description: The copper pheasant (Syrmaticus soemmerringii), also known as Soemmerring's pheasant or , is a pheasant endemic to the Japanese archipelago.

children.name: Tetrao
children.description: A genus of 2 capercaillie species from the boreal and mountain forests of Eurasia, including the Western Capercaillie, the largest grouse in the world and famed for its elaborate gurgling lekking song.

children.name: Tetrao urogallus
children.description: The western capercaillie, also known as the Eurasian capercaillie, wood grouse, heather cock, cock-of-the-woods, or simply capercaillie, is a heavy member of the grouse tribe and the largest of all extant grouse species. Found across Europe and the Palearctic, this primarily-ground-dwelling forest grouse is renowned for its courtship display. The bird shows extreme sexual dimorphism, with males nearly twice the size of females.

children.name: Tetraogallus
children.description: A genus of 5 snowcock species inhabiting the highest alpine zones of central Asia and the Caucasus—from the Himalayas to the Altai—among the world's highest-altitude birds, capable of living at elevations above 5,000 m.

children.name: Tetraogallus altaicus
children.description: The Altai snowcock (Tetraogallus altaicus) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.

children.name: Tetraogallus caspius
children.description: The Caspian snowcock (Tetraogallus caspius) is a snowcock in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes, gallinaceous birds.

children.name: Tetraogallus caucasicus
children.description: thumb| Tetraogallus caucasicus - [[MHNT]].

children.name: Tetraogallus himalayensis
children.description: The Himalayan snowcock (Tetraogallus himalayensis) is a snowcock in the pheasant family Phasianidae found across the Himalayan ranges and parts of the adjoining Pamir range of Asia.

children.name: Tetraogallus tibetanus
children.description: thumb|Tibetan Snowcock in Zingral Transit Check Post, Leh, Ladakh The Tibetan snowcock (Tetraogallus tibetanus) is a bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes, gallinaceous birds.

children.name: Tetraophasis
children.description: A genus of 2 monal-partridge species found in the high-altitude bamboo and rhododendron forests of southwestern China and Tibet, intermediate in appearance between snowcocks and true pheasants.

children.name: Tetrastes
children.description: A genus of 2 hazel-grouse species from Eurasia—the widespread Hazel Grouse and the Chinese Grouse—small, secretive forest grouse of mixed and deciduous taiga from Western Europe to East Asia.

children.name: Tetrastes bonasia
children.description: The hazel grouse (Tetrastes bonasia), sometimes called the hazel hen, is one of the smaller members of the grouse tribe of birds.

children.name: Tetrastes sewerzowi
children.description: The Chinese grouse (Tetrastes sewerzowi), also known as Severtzov's grouse, is the smallest grouse in the world.

children.name: Tragopan
children.description: A genus of 5 horned pheasant species from the Himalayan and Chinese mountain forests, the males displaying brilliantly spotted and wattled plumage and colorful inflatable facial lappets during courtship.

children.name: Tragopan melanocephalus
children.description: The western tragopan or western horned tragopan (Tragopan melanocephalus) is a medium-sized brightly plumed landfowl found along the range of Western Himalayas from north-eastern districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in northern Pakistan in the west to Uttarakhand within India to the east.

children.name: Tragopan satyra
children.description: The satyr tragopan (Tragopan satyra) also known as the crimson horned pheasant, is a pheasant found in the Himalayan reaches of India, Tibet, Nepal and Bhutan.

children.name: Tropicoperdix
children.description: A genus of 2 green-legged partridge species from the tropical forests of mainland Southeast Asia, recently separated from Arborophila based on morphological and molecular distinctions.

children.name: Tympanuchus
children.description: A genus of 3 prairie-chicken and sharp-tailed grouse species endemic to the grasslands and open country of central North America, known for spectacular group lekking displays with inflated colored air sacs.

children.name: Tympanuchus cupido
children.description: The greater prairie-chicken or pinnated grouse (Tympanuchus cupido), sometimes called a boomer, is a large bird in the grouse tribe.

children.name: Tympanuchus pallidicinctus
children.description: The lesser prairie-chicken is a species in the grouse tribe.

children.name: Xenoperdix
children.description: A genus of 2 Tanzanian forest partridge species confined to the montane forests of the Eastern Arc Mountains of Tanzania, among the most recently discovered and least-known African gamebirds.

children.name: Numida
children.description: The best-known guineafowl genus, domesticated for millennia and widely introduced beyond its native range. Characterised by the bare crowned head and the characteristic spotted or pearl-grey plumage that gives the domesticated forms their familiar look.

children.name: Numida meleagris
children.description: The helmeted guinea fowl (Numida meleagris) is the best known of the guinea fowl bird family, Numididae, and the only member of the genus Numida.

children.name: Guttera
children.description: Distinguished from other guineafowl by a prominent black crest of curly feathers on the crown. The two species occupy forest and woodland habitats in sub-Saharan Africa, with subtle plumage differences distinguishing the crested and plumed forms.

children.name: Acryllium
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the striking vulturine guineafowl, the largest and most colourful member of the family. The bare-skinned face and elongated neck feathers give it a distinctly vulturine appearance, and it inhabits dry savanna in East Africa.

children.name: Acryllium vulturinum
children.description: The vulturine guineafowl (Acryllium vulturinum) is the largest extant species of guinea fowl.

children.name: Agelastes
children.description: A small genus of two guineafowl species that lack the typical spotted plumage of the family, instead having unpatterned black or grey-brown feathers. Both are forest-dwelling and more secretive than other guineafowl.

children.name: Aepypodius
children.description: Aepypodius — a genus of megapodes in the family Megapodiidae.

children.name: Aepypodius arfakianus
children.description: The wattled brushturkey is a species of bird in the family Megapodiidae found year-round in New Guinea. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Aepypodius bruijnii
children.description: The Waigeo brushturkey or Bruijn's brushturkey, is a large brownish-black megapode with a bare red facial skin, red comb, maroon rump, and chestnut brown below. There are two elongated red wattles on the back of the head and a long wattle on the foredeck. Both sexes are similar.

children.name: Alectura
children.description: Large, dark-plumaged megapodes with a prominent bare red head and a laterally compressed tail. They are widespread in eastern Australia and are famous for building enormous incubation mounds.

children.name: Alectura lathami
children.description: The Australian brushturkey, Australian brush-turkey, or gweela (Alectura lathami), also commonly called the bush turkey, scrub turkey, or just brushturkey, is a large mound-building bird of the family Megapodiidae.

children.name: Eulipoa
children.description: A monotypic genus of megapode endemic to the Moluccas.

children.name: Eulipoa wallacei
children.description: The Moluccan megapode (Eulipoa wallacei), also known as Wallace's scrubfowl, Moluccan scrubfowl or painted megapode, is a small, approximately 31 cm long, olive-brown megapode.

children.name: Leipoa
children.description: A monotypic genus of shy, intricately patterned megapodes that inhabit the arid mallee scrublands of southern Australia. They are renowned for their precisely regulated incubation mounds.

children.name: Macrocephalon
children.description: A monotypic genus endemic to Sulawesi, instantly recognisable by the prominent helmet-like casque on its head. It is one of the most distinctive and endangered megapodes.

children.name: Megapodius
children.description: A widespread genus of medium-sized, drab-plumaged megapodes found across Southeast Asia, Australasia and the Pacific islands. They are named for their habit of scratching through deep forest litter.

children.name: Megapodius bernsteinii
children.description: The Sula megapode or Sula scrubfowl (Megapodius bernsteinii) is a species of bird in the family Megapodiidae.

children.name: Megapodius cumingii
children.description: The Philippine megapode (Megapodius cumingii), also known as the Philippine scrubfowl or the Tabon scrubfowl, is a species of bird in the family Megapodiidae.

children.name: Megapodius decollatus
children.description: The New Guinea scrubfowl or New Guinea megapode is a species of bird in the family Megapodiidae. It is found in New Guinea, mostly in the northern half. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Megapodius eremita
children.description: The Melanesian scrubfowl or Melanesian megapode is a megapode species that is endemic to islands within Melanesia. The Melanesian scrubfowl has a unique strategy of egg incubation in which it relies on environmental heat sources. This bird species is culturally important for Indigenous peoples in Melanesia.

children.name: Megapodius freycinet
children.description: The dusky megapode (Megapodius freycinet), also known as dusky scrubfowl or common megapode, is a medium-sized, approximately 41 cm (16 in) long, blackish bird with a short pointed crest, bare red facial skin, dark legs, brown irises, and a dark brown and yellow bill.

children.name: Megapodius geelvinkianus
children.description: The Biak scrubfowl or Biak megapode (Megapodius geelvinkianus) is a species of bird in the family Megapodiidae.

children.name: Megapodius laferrieri
children.description: A scrubfowl from the Sulu Archipelago.

children.name: Megapodius laperouse
children.description: The Micronesian megapode or Micronesian scrubfowl is a megapode which inhabits islands of the Western Pacific Ocean.

children.name: Megapodius layardi
children.description: The Vanuatu megapode or Vanuatu scrubfowl is a species of bird in the family Megapodiidae. It was formerly known as the New Hebrides scrubfowl. It is found only in Vanuatu.

children.name: Megapodius leakeyorum
children.description: A scrubfowl from the Sula Islands.

children.name: Megapodius nicobariensis
children.description: The Nicobar megapode or Nicobar scrubfowl (Megapodius nicobariensis) is a megapode endemic to the Nicobar Islands of India.

children.name: Megapodius pritchardii
children.description: The Tongan megapode (Megapodius pritchardii) is a species of bird in the megapode family, Megapodiidae, currently endemic to Tonga.

children.name: Megapodius tenebrosus
children.description: A scrubfowl endemic to the Tanimbar Islands, Indonesia.

children.name: Megapodius tenimberensis
children.description: The Tanimbar megapode or Tanimbar scrubfowl is a small megapode endemic to the Tanimbar Islands of Indonesia. It is sometimes considered to be a subspecies of the orange-footed scrubfowl, Megapodius reinwardt.

children.name: Megapodius wallacei
children.description: The Moluccan megapode (Eulipoa wallacei), also known as Wallace's scrubfowl, Moluccan scrubfowl or painted megapode, is a small, approximately 31 cm long, olive-brown megapode.

children.name: Aburria
children.description: Aburria — a genus of curassows & guans in the family Cracidae.

children.name: Chamaepetes
children.description: Mid-sized, slender guans with a glossy black plumage and bare blue facial skin. They are restricted to montane forests of Central America and the northern Andes.

children.name: Chamaepetes goudotii
children.description: The sickle-winged guan is a species of bird in the chachalaca, guan, and curassow family Cracidae. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Chamaepetes unicolor
children.description: The black guan (Chamaepetes unicolor) is a species of bird in the chachalaca, guan, and curassow family Cracidae.

children.name: Crax
children.description: Large, heavy-bodied curassows with a prominent curled crest of feathers and brightly coloured bills and ceres. Males are predominantly black while females are often barred or rufous.

children.name: Crax rubra
children.description: The great curassow (Crax rubra) is a large, pheasant-like bird from the Neotropical rainforests, its range extending from eastern Mexico, through Central America to western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador.

children.name: Crax alector
children.description: The black curassow (Crax alector), also known as the smooth-billed curassow and the crested curassow, is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.

children.name: Crax globulosa
children.description: The wattled curassow (Crax globulosa) is a threatened member of the family Cracidae, the curassows, guans, and chachalacas.

children.name: Mitu
children.description: Mitu — a genus of curassows & guans in the family Cracidae.

children.name: Nothocrax
children.description: Nothocrax — a genus of curassows & guans in the family Cracidae.

children.name: Nothocrax urumutum
children.description: The nocturnal curassow is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows. It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

children.name: Oreophasis
children.description: Oreophasis — a genus of curassows & guans in the family Cracidae.

children.name: Ortalis
children.description: Medium-sized, long-tailed cracids with slender builds and a raucous, far-carrying call that gives them their onomatopoeic name. They are among the most widespread and adaptable members of the family.

children.name: Ortalis atriceps
children.description: A chachalaca with brown head, found from Mexico to Honduras.

children.name: Ortalis canicollis
children.description: The Chaco chachalaca (Ortalis canicollis) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.

children.name: Ortalis motmot
children.description: The little chachalaca (Ortalis motmot) is a bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.

children.name: Ortalis vetula
children.description: The plain chachalaca (Ortalis vetula) is a large bird in the chachalaca, guan and curassow family Cracidae.

children.name: Ortalis wagneri
children.description: A chachalaca endemic to western Mexico.

children.name: Palaeonossax
children.description: Palaeonossax — a genus of curassows & guans in the family Cracidae.

children.name: Pauxi
children.description: Easily identified by the distinctive, bulbous casque on the forehead, which is hard and bone-like in texture. These large, terrestrial birds inhabit montane and foothill forests of South America.

children.name: Pauxi pauxi
children.description: The helmeted curassow (Pauxi pauxi) or northern helmeted curassow, is a large terrestrial bird in the family Cracidae found in the subtropical cloud-forest in steep, mountainous regions of western Venezuela and northern Colombia.

children.name: Penelope
children.description: Medium-to-large guans with a bare throat wattle and a dark brown or blackish plumage with subtle white streaking on the neck and breast. They are arboreal and highly vocal.

children.name: Penelope barbata
children.description: The bearded guan (Penelope barbata) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.

children.name: Penelope marail
children.description: The marail guan or Cayenne guan (Penelope marail) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.

children.name: Penelope ortoni
children.description: The Baudó guan (Penelope ortoni) is a species of bird from the family Cracidae.

children.name: Penelope perspicax
children.description: The Cauca guan is a bird in the chachalaca, guan and curassow family, Cracidae. It is a large guan, and like most guans leads a mostly arboreal life in humid forests, where it forages for fruit and leaves. The Cauca guan is endemic to Colombia's Cauca River valley.

children.name: Penelope purpurascens
children.description: The crested guan (Penelope purpurascens) is a Near Threatened species in an ancient group of birds of the family Cracidae, which are related to the Australasian megapodes or mound builders (Megapodiidae).

children.name: Penelopina
children.description: Penelopina — a genus of curassows & guans in the family Cracidae.

children.name: Pipile
children.description: Pipile — a genus of curassows & guans in the family Cracidae.

children.name: Callipepla
children.description: Elegant quail with a distinctive forward-curving plume of feathers on the crown, composed of six upright feathers. They are adapted to arid and semi-arid landscapes of western North America.

children.name: Callipepla californica
children.description: The California quail, also known as the California valley quail or Valley quail, is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family, inhabiting western North America. It is the state bird of California.

children.name: Callipepla squamata
children.description: The scaled quail (Callipepla squamata), also commonly called blue quail or cottontop, is a species of the New World quail family.

children.name: Colinus
children.description: Small, plump quail with mottled brown plumage and a distinctive white or buff facial stripe. They are highly social, forming coveys that forage together on the ground.

children.name: Colinus virginianus
children.description: The northern bobwhite (Colinus virginianus), also known as the Virginia quail or (in its home range) bobwhite quail, is a ground-dwelling bird native to Canada, the United States, Mexico, and Cuba, with introduced populations elsewhere in the Caribbean, Europe, and Asia.

children.name: Colinus nigrogularis
children.description: The Yucatan bobwhite or black-throated bobwhite (Colinus nigrogularis) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Colinus cristatus
children.description: The crested bobwhite (Colinus cristatus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Cyrtonyx
children.description: Distinctive, stocky quail with an extremely short tail and an intricately patterned plumage of black, white and chestnut. They are among the most beautiful but secretive of the New World quail.

children.name: Cyrtonyx montezumae
children.description: The Montezuma quail (Cyrtonyx montezumae) is a stubby, secretive New World quail of Mexico and some nearby parts of the United States.

children.name: Cyrtonyx ocellatus
children.description: The ocellated quail is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

children.name: Dactylortyx
children.description: A monotypic genus of quail with a beautiful song.

children.name: Dactylortyx thoracicus
children.description: The singing quail (Dactylortyx thoracicus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail.

children.name: Dendrortyx
children.description: Dendrortyx — a genus of new world quail in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Dendrortyx barbatus
children.description: The bearded wood partridge is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It inhabits the Sierra Madre Oriental of Mexico.

children.name: Dendrortyx leucophrys
children.description: The buffy-crowned wood partridge is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found in Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Costa Rica and Nicaragua.

children.name: Dendrortyx macroura
children.description: The long-tailed wood partridge is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail. It is found only in Mexico.

children.name: Nanortyx
children.description: Nanortyx — a genus of new world quail in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Odontophorus
children.description: Stocky forest quail found in Central and South America.

children.name: Odontophorus guianensis
children.description: A wood quail from the Guiana Shield.

children.name: Odontophorus speciosus
children.description: The rufous-breasted wood quail is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae. It is found in Bolivia, Ecuador, and Peru primarily on the east side of the Andes between 800 and 2000m in elevation.

children.name: Odontophorus striolatus
children.description: A wood quail from the western Amazon.

children.name: Oreortyx
children.description: A monotypic genus of the largest New World quail, characterised by a long, straight black plume rising vertically from the crown. It is an expert runner and prefers rugged, mountainous terrain.

children.name: Oreortyx pictus
children.description: The mountain quail (Oreortyx pictus) is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family.

children.name: Philortyx
children.description: A monotypic genus of quail from western Mexico.

children.name: Philortyx fasciatus
children.description: The banded quail (Philortyx fasciatus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Ptilopachus
children.description: Ptilopachus — a genus of new world quail in the family Odontophoridae.

children.name: Ptilopachus petrosus
children.description: The stone partridge is a bird of the New World quail family. This largely brown bird, which commonly holds its tail raised, is found in scrubland and lightly wooded habitats, often near rocks, from Kenya and Ethiopia to Gambia.

children.name: Rhynchortyx
children.description: A monotypic genus of quail from Central and South America.
